minimal.description: Run a shell command inside an open workspace. Use only for tests, builds, git inspection, package scripts, search, file discovery, and directory inspection. In minimal tool mode, grep, glob, and ls are disabled; use command-line tools such as grep, rg, find, ls, and tree for those read-only inspection actions. Do not use bash to create or modify files. Do not use shell redirection, heredocs, tee, sed -i, perl -i, node/python/ruby scripts, or generated scripts to write project files; use edit for targeted changes and write for new files or full rewrites. Prefer read for direct file reads. Call open_workspace first and pass workspaceId. This is powerful local execution and should only be exposed behind strong authentication.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Defaults to 30, max 300.

workingDirectory.description: Optional working directory relative to the workspace root. Defaults to the workspace root.

Each oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file; merge nearby changes into one edit and keep oldText as small as possible while still unique. Call open_workspace first and pass workspaceId.

minimal.description: Open or resume a local project directory as a coding workspace. Checkout mode reuses the most recently active workspace for the same path by default, including after its in-memory metadata was released. Set forceNew only when a distinct checkout session is explicitly required. Worktree mode always creates an isolated managed Git worktree. Returns a persistent workspaceId, loaded root project instructions, and nested instruction file paths.

baseRef.description: Git ref to base a worktree on. Only used with mode="worktree". Defaults to HEAD.

forceNew.description: Checkout mode only. Defaults to false so the latest workspace for the same path is resumed. Set true only when a distinct workspaceId is explicitly needed.

mode.description: Defaults to checkout. Use checkout to work in the actual directory. Use worktree to create an isolated managed Git worktree for parallel work.

path.description: Absolute path, or a leading-tilde home path such as ~/project, to a local project directory inside an allowed root.

minimal.description: Read a file inside an open workspace. Use this for file inspection instead of shell commands like cat or sed. Call open_workspace first and pass workspaceId. UTF-8 text is streamed in pages up to 1 MiB (default 20,000 lines). Follow the returned byteOffset to continue; do not combine byteOffset with offset. Images up to 16 MiB use the image reader. Use this tool to inspect relevant AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files listed by open_workspace before working in nested directories.

byteOffset.description: Zero-based byte cursor returned by the previous page; omit offset when using this.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read.

offset.description: 1-indexed line number to start reading from.

path.description: File path to read, relative to the workspace root.

minimal.description: Release this workspace's in-memory metadata only when the user explicitly requests resource release or the workspace is known to be unused for a long time. The workspace session remains persisted and recoverable: if the conversation continues, pass the same workspaceId to any workspace tool and DevSpace will restore it automatically. This does not delete files or worktrees, stop commands, revoke the workspaceId, close the MCP transport, or stop the shared server.
